Student Ability Evaluation AI Engine

The proposed system, StudentAbility AI, will evaluate students across five subjects:

  • Mathematics

  • Physics

  • English

  • Chemistry

  • Biology

It will estimate individual ability, identify strengths and weaknesses, measure proficiency by topic, and recommend which areas require further assessment or improvement.

The system will support both students and teachers through a Python REST API, with separate MySQL and MongoDB implementations.

Part 1 — Proposed AI algorithm

I recommend a Bayesian Item Response Theory (IRT) engine, with adaptive question selection and periodic parameter calibration.

Unlike a traditional grading algorithm that only calculates the percentage of correct answers, IRT considers question difficulty and how effectively each question distinguishes different ability levels.

1.2 Bayesian student-ability estimation

After each answered question, the engine estimates ability using a standard-normal prior and the observed responses:

θ^s=arg⁡max⁡θ[−θ22+∑q=1n(ysqlog⁡psq+(1−ysq)log⁡(1−psq))]\hat\theta_s=\arg\max_\theta\left[ -\frac{\theta^2}{2} +\sum_{q=1}^{n} \left(y_{sq}\log p_{sq}+ (1-y_{sq})\log(1-p_{sq})\right) \right]θ^s​=argθmax​[−2θ2​+q=1∑n​(ysq​logpsq​+(1−ysq​)log(1−psq​))]

The engine also calculates an approximate uncertainty interval. This matters because a student answering three questions correctly should not automatically receive the same confidence rating as a student consistently performing well across thirty questions.

1.3 Subject and topic evaluation

Each subject has its own ability estimate. Topic-level estimates give teachers more actionable evidence.

The system will distinguish observed accuracy, estimated ability, and confidence in that estimate.

1.4 Adaptive assessment

The next-question algorithm will:

  1. Retrieve the student's previous answers.

  2. Estimate subject proficiency and topic coverage.

  3. Identify topics needing additional evidence.

  4. Select an unseen question with high expected statistical information.

  5. Update the student's ability estimate after the response.

The question information function is:

Iq(θ)=aq2Pq(θ)(1−Pq(θ))I_q(\theta)=a_q^2P_q(\theta)(1-P_q(\theta))Iq​(θ)=aq2​Pq​(θ)(1−Pq​(θ))

This supports adaptive assessment without requiring every student to answer the same sequence of questions.

1.5 Continuous model improvement

Two learning mechanisms are planned:

  • Online updating: Student ability estimates change as new answers arrive.

  • Offline calibration: With sufficient responses from different students, the engine can re-estimate question difficulty and discrimination using regularized optimization.

Initial question parameters will be provisional. They must be empirically validated before the system is used for consequential academic decisions.

Part 3 — Python AI engines

Complete Python source project

ZIP · MySQL and MongoDB adapters · REST API · tests · sample data

Download Complete AI Engine

The archive contains separate MySQL and MongoDB database implementations that share the same evaluation algorithm.

MySQL

SQLAlchemy + PyMySQL

Stores students, questions, responses, and proficiency estimates in relational tables.

MongoDB

PyMongo

Stores equivalent information in MongoDB collections and supports the same assessment API.

Both engines implement subject and topic evaluation, adaptive question selection, confidence estimates, and offline recalibration.

Running the project on Linux

After extracting the ZIP, run:

Bash
cd student_ability_ai
cp .env.example .env

# Edit .env to set your database
# configuration and API secrets.

docker compose up -d mysql mongodb

python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate

pip install -r requirements.txt

python -m app.seed --demo

uvicorn app.api:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000

For MongoDB, change DB_BACKEND=mysql to DB_BACKEND=mongodb in .env, then seed its separate database and start the API.

You can access the interactive API documentation at http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs.

Validation status

The package was checked after extraction: 9 automated tests passed and 1 optional MongoDB test was skipped because its test dependencies were unavailable in this environment. The SQL-compatible API tests and synthetic calibration test passed. Live MySQL and MongoDB server connectivity still needs to be verified on your deployment server.

The initial question parameters are illustrative, not empirically calibrated. Before using this with real students for consequential decisions, you will need institution-specific question calibration, psychometric validation, and role-based access controls.

The next practical step is to map this engine to your school's existing student, examination, subject, and question-bank data so that it can evaluate actual student performance rather than demonstration responses.
